newsitem.title: USA: Cold, snowy Friday seen for northern U.S. Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Cold, snowy Friday seen for northern U.S. Midwest.

text.p: Meteorologists predicted a cold, snowy Friday for the northern U.S. Midwest but temperatures were expected to moderate next week.
"We have developed a west to east storm track across the northern half of the United States from the Pacific all the way across," said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster with Weather Express Inc.

That system will bring unsettled weather to the U.S. Midwest about every two days, he said. The first storm was expected to dump up to six inches of snow on Friday across northeast Iowa, Minnesota and Wisconsin.
The system will bring rain and freezing rain to the southern Midwest. Chicago should be on the border with a mix of freezing rain and snow forecast for Friday.
Temperatures were expected to drop behind the storm front. Cold weather had already reached the Dakotas on Thursday.
Temperatures Thursday morning dropped to -18 Fahrenheit in Fargo, N.D, and -7 F in Sioux Falls, S.D., said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
"It doesn't look like the coldest air mass of all time but there is colder weather settling across the Midwest today with highs in the upper teens to 20s," he said.
Temperatures were expected to turn colder over the weekend with much below normal readings seen Sunday morning for areas spanning the northern Plains and Midwest.
"The Midwest is going to turn much colder Sunday morning with single digits in Chicago," Burgio said. "That high moves eastward and it warms up a bit behind that."

Meanwhile, the southern Plains should see dry weather with readings near normal but another cold front could drop temperatures into the teens F Sunday morning, Gesser said. "From the Nebraska grain areas to the Texas Panhandle, it will be bone dry," he said.
Sunday morning lows will range from the single digits in Nebraska to the upper teens and 20s in the Texas Panhandle, he said.
